items.title: Lou Marini interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 15, 2023
items.q: But I remember talking to Dizzy about that. And Dizzy said it’s only happened to him a few times in his life.

ctx.x: He used to do a lot of jazz, a big guy, had a beard, I worked for him a bunch of times. His name is escaping me now, but he told me he saw Trane one night with the band with Pharaoh Sanders and towards the end of Trane’s life. And he said at one point Trane stopped playing and was beating on his chest in the music you know. Those glimpses that we have of — I mentioned earlier something about when you’re sometimes when you’re really playing and you’re in a different place if your ego comes in you crash to earth.…

Is there something about the times and the state of society that you think might make what you’re describing very hard to ever reproduce? And the reason I ask that is I spoke to Rashied Ali once and was trying to get at the attitude of the musicians when he played in late Coltrane’s life. And he just kept saying, “Listen, the times were different. The bebop people had their time, this was our time.” So I’m not asking this question very well but do you think that the time and space that John Coltrane was doing…
